headline: Futures rally ~1% as a US-Iran strike pause deflates the oil risk premium that had dominated markets all week.
stance: The single biggest variable of the last two weeks — Middle East-driven oil prices — has just printed a sharp reversal. Brent fell roughly 7% overnight after the US paused strikes against Iran, and that single data point is doing most of the work lifting futures and weakening the dollar this morning. The relief is real, but it arrives into a week packed with three hyperscaler earnings (Amazon, Meta, Microsoft), Apple, and a live FOMC decision on Wednesday — so do not mistake a one-day geopolitical exhale for a clear-air climb.

news.head: US-Iran Strike Pause
news.body: The US paused an almost two-week run of strikes against Iran over the weekend, triggering a broad relief rally: equities up, oil down sharply, bonds bid, dollar softer.

news.head: Brent Crude Plunges
news.body: Brent fell as much as 7.4% in early overnight trade, briefly dipping below $90/bbl before partially recovering toward ~$93-96 — giving back the war premium that had pushed it above $100 last week.

news.head: FOMC Begins July 28-29
news.body: The Federal Reserve's two-day meeting starts tomorrow; futures markets price roughly a 36-38% chance of a 25 bp hike at Wednesday's decision (2pm ET), with a hold still the base case at ~62%.

news.head: Durable Goods Beat
news.body: June US durable goods orders rose 1.6% (May had contracted 4.5%), with the core capital-goods proxy up 1.4% vs. 1.3% expected — reinforcing the 'higher-for-longer' rate narrative.

news.head: Alphabet AI-Spend Shock
news.body: Last week Alphabet delivered solid revenues but alarmed investors with surging AI infrastructure costs and negative free cash flow, sinking its stock and dragging the Nasdaq down ~1.1% on Friday.

news.head: Mega-Cap Earnings Gauntlet
news.body: Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft report Wednesday-Thursday this week, with Apple and Qualcomm also on deck — the busiest stretch of earnings this quarter.

news.head: CXMT Shanghai IPO
news.body: Chinese memory-chip maker CXMT lists on the Shanghai STAR Market today after raising $8.6 bn — Asia's largest IPO of 2026 — adding a fresh lens on semiconductor sector dynamics.

news.head: BOJ Meeting Also This Week
news.body: The Bank of Japan holds its policy meeting July 30-31, injecting a separate volatility risk into USD/JPY, which closed Friday at a near-extreme 163.79 yen per dollar (prior cash close).

implications: The oil-driven inflation shock that pushed the 10-year yield to a 1.5-year high last week is now partially unwinding — watch whether bond yields follow crude lower or stay sticky on the durable-goods beat.
A Fed hold Wednesday removes the single biggest near-term equity headwind, but hawkish guidance or a surprise hike would reprice the entire rate path and pressure the CAPE-40 market hard.
Nasdaq futures lead the pre-market bounce (+~1.4%) but the index still carries the Alphabet hangover; investors will demand Amazon/Meta/Microsoft prove AI spend has a return, not just a cost.
Dollar softening on the Iran pause benefits commodities and EM; EUR/USD (prior close 1.1375) presses toward 1.14 while the extreme-percentile yen (163.79) keeps BOJ intervention risk alive.

Positioning: S&P 500 futures specs are at an extended long (85th percentile) — a contrarian warning for the index. Russell 2000 specs are at the opposite extreme: speculators have almost no bullish bets left — a contrarian floor. In FX, Euro and GBP specs are both in extended short territory — contrarian-bullish for those pairs if dollar weakness continues. In commodities, Copper (96th pctile) and Wheat (98th pctile) specs are heavily positioned long — contrarian warnings. WTI specs are at the 13th percentile — speculators have almost no bullish bets left, a contrarian floor even as price falls today.

watch.head: Brent Intraday Level
watch.body: Whether Brent stabilizes above $90 or collapses further determines whether inflation fears fully defuse into the FOMC — the prior cash close was $98.38.

watch.head: 10-Year Yield Direction
watch.body: The prior cash close was 4.69%; a move below 4.60% on the oil drop would ease pressure on rate-sensitive equities, but the durable-goods beat argues against a large rally.

watch.head: FOMC Statement Tone (Wed)
watch.body: Even a hold can be hawkish if Chair Warsh signals September is live — watch the press conference at 2:30pm ET Wednesday for any change in inflation language.

watch.head: USD/JPY vs. BOJ
watch.body: The yen is at a 3-year extreme (99.9th percentile at 163.79 prior close); BOJ meets July 30-31 and any hawkish surprise could trigger a sharp yen rally and cross-asset volatility.

watch.head: Hyperscaler Earnings Tone
watch.body: After Alphabet's AI-capex scare, the market is asking Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft to show free-cash-flow discipline — results land Wednesday-Thursday after the bell.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: 10-year Treasury yield: 4.69% (prior cash close); the prior week's surge to a 1.5-year high was driven by oil-inflation fears — those fears are now partly deflating on the Iran pause.
2-year yield: 4.33% (prior cash close); yield curve (2s10s) is just +36 bps — still historically flat, meaning the bond market is not pricing a clean growth recovery.
Real rates: 2.43% (prior cash close) — the real cost of money remains among the highest in years, a persistent headwind for growth stocks and housing.
10-year breakeven inflation: 2.26% (prior cash close) — markets expect inflation to drift only modestly above the Fed's 2% target, but another oil spike would change that quickly.
FOMC July 28-29: futures price a ~36-38% chance of a 25 bp hike, with current Fed funds target at 3.50-3.75%; most economists expect a hold, with September seen as the next live meeting.
June durable goods orders rose 1.6% (vs. May's -4.5% drop), with the core business-investment proxy up 1.4% — a 'higher-for-longer' data point that limits any bond rally.
Financial conditions remain accommodative: the ANFCI reads -0.55 and the STLFSI -0.70 (both as of Jul 17) — loose by historical standards despite elevated yields.
Term premium on 10-year Treasuries: 77.9 bps (as of Jul 17) — investors are demanding extra compensation to hold long bonds, reflecting inflation uncertainty and heavy supply.
sections.positioning: 3M SOFR specs are at the 4th percentile — speculators have almost no bullish bets left in short-term rates, a contrarian-bullish lean for rate futures (i.e., specs are positioned for rates to stay high, but the position is stretched).

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: S&P 500: 7,411.98 (prior cash close Fri Jul 25); ES futures are indicated ~+0.8% pre-market, pointing to an open near 7,470.
Nasdaq-100: 24,975.82 (prior cash close); NQ futures are indicated ~+1.4% pre-market — the biggest bounce among major indices on relief from lower oil and a softer dollar.
Dow Jones: 51,947.25 (prior cash close); YM futures are indicated ~+0.8% pre-market.
VIX: 18.58 (prior cash close) — elevated but not panicked; the VXN (Nasdaq vol) at 28.39 reflects the lingering AI-earnings uncertainty premium in tech.
SKEW index: 147.3 (prior cash close) — options traders are paying up for downside protection, signaling caution beneath the surface rally.
Breadth: 63.4% of S&P 500 stocks trade above their 50-day average; only 42.6% of Nasdaq-100 stocks do — the Nasdaq's internal weakness is notable despite headline-index strength.

CAPE ratio: 40.46 (prior cash close) — valuations remain stretched historically; the equity risk premium (ERP) is -2.0% (as of Jun 30), meaning stocks offer less yield than bonds — an unusual and vulnerable configuration.
Alphabet's AI-capex scare last week sent the Mag-7 ETF down more than 5% for the week while semiconductor ETFs rose — a rotation from AI spenders to AI enablers worth watching this earnings week.
sections.positioning: S&P 500 futures specs are at an extended long (85th percentile) — speculators are heavily positioned long, a contrarian warning. Russell 2000 specs are at the 4th percentile — speculators have almost no bullish bets left, a contrarian floor for small-caps. VIX specs are also at an extended short (10th percentile), consistent with the low-vol complacency embedded in an 18.58 VIX.

single_name.note: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) — world's largest contract chipmaker; company insiders have been buying, dark-pool and options activity is live, stock trades above its 200-day line. Sits at the intersection of the AI-capex rotation (semis benefit when hyperscalers spend) and the US-Iran/Strait of Hormuz geopolitical risk. Signal is fresh.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: HY-IG spread: 277 bps (as of Jul 23) — high-yield bonds are not yet pricing stress; credit is behaving well relative to the equity volatility of last week.
IG option-adjusted spread: 79 bps (as of Jul 23) — investment-grade credit spreads are tight, consistent with loose financial conditions.
FRA-OIS and SOFR-OIS: both 1 bp (as of Jul 23) — interbank funding markets are calm; no plumbing stress visible.
Commercial paper spread: 18 bps (as of Jul 24) — short-term corporate funding is operating normally.
Bank reserves: $3,062 bn (as of Jul 22); Fed balance sheet growing just 1.35% YoY — system liquidity is ample but not expanding rapidly.
Treasury General Account (TGA): $829.6 bn (as of Jul 22) — a large TGA can be a drain on bank reserves if the Treasury draws it down; worth monitoring through the debt-ceiling cycle.
Reverse repo (RRP): $0.7 bn (as of Jul 24) — effectively zero, confirming excess liquidity has moved out of the Fed's facility and into markets.
Bank credit growth: 6.4% YoY (as of Jul 15) — healthy, not overheating; consistent with a slow-but-positive macro backdrop.

single_name.note: Five Star Bancorp (FSBC) — California commercial bank; 2 separate company-insider buying signals fired, stock trades above its 200-day line, dark-pool and options flow both live. Short interest at 3.15 days-to-cover — shorts are present but not extreme, limiting squeeze risk. Signal is fresh.
